indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A dazzling performance at a trial in a criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a description of the court case, but it signals an anagram of COURT CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to flash or glitter, a literary synonym for sparkle.

definitions.meaning: husks and waste separated from grain are worthless refuse
light-hearted teasing talk is also known by this word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both worthless husks of grain and playful joking talk.

clue.text: Equip mother to play part in complicated arrangement

parts.note: to rig is to fit out or equip
ma is an informal word for mother
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A family drama where Mum is kitted out to take a role in an elaborate production.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, complicated procedure, a fussy arrangement.

clue.text: Burial at sea is in — so American and wholesome

indicators.note: the anagrammed word is in the middle of the two-letter word so

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of burial are jumbled

explanation.surface: A burial at sea is presented as a clean, healthy American custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' places the jumbled burial inside so; the surface's funeral at sea hides that 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salubrious means health-giving or pleasant, close in sense to wholesome.

clue.text: Not a drug that's done any wrong?

definitions.text: Not a drug that's done any wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means set awry, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A question about a harmless medicine that has never caused trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DONE ANY. The whole clue also defines: an innocuous thing is one that has done no wrong, while the word also names a painkilling drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means inoffensive and harmless, though the noun names a soothing painkiller, hence the playful negation.

parts.note: ex means former, once
a tin is a container or vessel
the word caught shortened to an abbreviation of two letters

explanation.surface: A ship that sank long ago, taken by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species or volcano is dead, no longer living or active.

parts.note: past means gone by

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian dish of dough that makes a meal.

clue.text: Part of organ that's seed bearing

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed
E is east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Part of a plant organ that carries seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A church organ sounds through its many pipes, each one a component.

indicators.note: about here means around in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stories concerning Saint Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name, but it is the slang verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick something is to steal it.

clue.text: Ayckbourn circumvents ban for star of "The Bull"

indicators.note: circumvents means goes around, so the playwright's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Alan Ayckbourn is an English playwright
to debar is to ban

explanation.surface: A playwright gets round a ban to cast a star in a play called The Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the brightest star in Taurus, the constellation of the Bull.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a gel is a colloidal suspension

explanation.surface: A ghost that gets someone suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit.

definitions.meaning: a picnic is a food spread laid out of doors, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The word means spread wide, and split in two describes a meal laid out in the open air.

clue.text: Elaborate old pulpit covered by insects

indicators.note: the pulpit is enclosed by the insect words

parts.note: a fly is an insect
an ambo is a raised pulpit in early churches
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An ornate antique pulpit crawling with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts the pulpit word inside the first insect; an ambo is the raised reading desk of early churches, a word most solvers meet only in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and ornate, elaborate in style.

clue.text: Shed tears if, say, onion's about

indicators.note: about signals the word is turned round

parts.note: an onion is an example of a bulb

explanation.surface: Weeping caused by chopping onions.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is to cry noisily, an informal way of saying shed tears.

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A fanciful proposal to crossbreed lions with bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animal, but it signals an anagram of MERGE LIONS; the whole clue also describes crossbreeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To mongrelise is to cross different breeds, as merging lions and bats would do.

indicators.note: casing means wrapped round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to prove is to show
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone offering to provide a display case.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide is to supply, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: put in means one piece is inserted into another

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An election boast: I'd install the leader here.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, a leader.

indicators.note: capturing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other
about signals the word for crack is turned round

parts.note: a report is a loud bang or crack
zilch means nothing, shown as O

explanation.surface: A soldier who has made a wisecrack about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a joke; it is the bang of a gun, REPORT, which 'about' turns to TROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Likely to have concert with one chorus

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert
I is the Roman numeral one
to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A concert where a solo singer joins in with the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Promising describes something likely to succeed, showing good prospects.

parts.note: a river has banks, and the Exe is a river in Devon
cute can mean clever or shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever banker making an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword trick for a river, here the Exe in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to carry it out, which is what execute means.

indicators.note: bouncy suggests the letters are bounced around into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child finds a bouncy castle springy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncy' rearranges CASTLE together with I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic springs back into shape, which is resilient.

parts.note: a vague alert reads as one sounded in murky weather at sea

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's horn signal is sounded when visibility is poor, a warning in unclear conditions.

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: feral means wild
ED is short for editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: A union official angry with a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Federal describes a union of states, so it means belonging to a union.

parts.note: mass is held in church, which gives the word in
CH is short for church, where mass is said

explanation.surface: A question about where the mass of an object lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like physics, but it is the church service, said in CH (church).
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, a small measure.

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to ache is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: Treatment for an aching skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, a hiding place.

definitions.meaning: the cord of a candle that gives light
a tufted cotton material used for bedspreads

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the cord that burns in a candle and a tufted cotton fabric.

clue.text: Draw at sea gives king advantage

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A chess game drawn on a ship gives the king an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To kedge is to draw a ship along by hauling on a small anchor.

indicators.note: the answer becomes a word for fast if given a letter, so that letter is taken off

parts.note: fleet means fast

explanation.surface: Advice to sprint if you have enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer if given T would be FLEET, so FLEET loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to escape at speed from danger, as in running from a fire.

clue.text: Energy-saving steps involve a real cost

indicators.note: involve means entangle, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Climbing stairs saves energy but carries a real price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involve' rearranges A REAL COST. The definition is witty: moving stairs save the rider's energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a moving staircase, steps that spare the climber effort.

clue.text: One cover binds a long story

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: binds means wraps round, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A book cover bound around a long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan war is a very long narrative poem.

clue.text: Home counties are more than this

explanation.surface: The counties around London are bigger than this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, read as THE SE (the south-east).
